doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Other tracks on In the Beginning; Come Ye Disconsolate for his mother
summary: Brown and Laws go through Restoration, Reconciliation, Mean Lean, Gymnopedie and Come Ye Disconsolate, which he recorded for his mother.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And Morning, which is big Pancho Sanchez. He took that to the bank.
So, that session. Let’s see. What else did we do on In the Beginning. We did . . .
Restoration was written by a friend of mine who also wrote the New Earth Sonata for us.
Reconciliation was written by the piano player who wrote Morning Star.
Then Mean Lean, which was written by the flutist and the leader.
Here’s the second time we see this, at least on a date that you’re the leader on. Gymnopedie, no. 2, Satie.

Come Ye Disconsolate is something I did as a followup to – after having dedicated to my father, then this one’s for my mother. That’s one of her favorites. So that’s why I recorded Come Ye Disconsolate.
